web_evidence.title: Dead Reckoning | Penguin Random House Library Marketing
web_evidence.note: The publisher’s sustained Chapter 1 excerpt follows Sookie through the attic and Merlotte’s scenes using continuous narratorial “I,” “my,” and “we,” with no competing base person.

web_evidence.title: Ethel the Aardvark 154
web_evidence.note: Paula McGrath’s contemporaneous review explicitly says Dead Reckoning is in first person and discusses how that viewpoint restricts the book to Sookie’s thoughts and interactions.

web_evidence.title: The Southern Vampire Mysteries
web_evidence.note: The series overview includes Dead Reckoning in the novel sequence and explicitly identifies Sookie Stackhouse as the series’ first-person narrator.

search_log: Searched “Dead Reckoning Charlaine Harris excerpt first chapter publisher” and related author, publisher, library, Google Books, and official-site combinations.
Searched “Dead Reckoning Charlaine Harris first person narrator,” “point of view,” “narrated by,” and “Sookie perspective” for explicit structural descriptions.
Opened the Penguin Random House Library Marketing page and verified its sustained authorized Chapter 1 excerpt rather than relying on the search snippet.
Opened the FANAC-hosted Ethel the Aardvark review PDF and verified its explicit whole-book discussion of the first-person viewpoint.
Opened the Southern Vampire Mysteries series overview and verified that it identifies Sookie as the first-person narrator and lists Dead Reckoning as book 11.

The current Penguin Random House retail page advertised a sample but did not expose its prose in the opened page; Google Books provided bibliographic and preview metadata but no usable person evidence in the opened view.

The former Charlaine Harris official Chapter 1 URL was identified through contemporaneous links but was no longer directly accessible; an inaccessible interview result and plot-summary grammar were not used as evidence.

Targeted searches for epistolary, frame-narrative, multiple-narrator, alternating-person, and third-person exceptions found no credible indication that Dead Reckoning departs from Sookie’s first-person narration.
person_note: Numerous Goodreads passages from different scenes expose Sookie’s participating narration through “I,” “me,” “my,” and “we”; dialogue-only and grammatically unmarked passages were not allowed to vote mechanically. The authorized opening independently sustains the same voice, while an explicit whole-book review and the series structure corroborate that the limitation to Sookie persists beyond the opening. No evidence of sustained third-person, second-person, framed, or alternating sections was found, so isolated third-person references to other characters are ordinary descriptions within Sookie’s first-person narration.
